digest.component_or_area: MCP server error handling and CLI/library error classification
propositions: MCP tool failures currently surface as unstructured prose in exception text or ad-hoc partial shapes, lacking the machine error discriminator that the CLI emits via error_envelope

A single error_code_for(exc)->str classifier and KNOWN_ERROR_CODES frozenset must exist in the library so all three interfaces (library, CLI, MCP) emit identical codes for the same failure, verified by cross-interface tests

MCP must deliver structured error_envelope (error, message, input, exit_code) via McpEnvelopeError.__cause__ on raised ToolError, with JSON serializable via __str__, so agents can branch on machine error codes without pattern-matching English

TicketNotFoundError must be a distinct ReadError subclass raised only at genuine not-found sites (reads.py:310/313), leaving the message-keyed CLI discriminator (reads_cli.py:410) and deps_failed path (reads.py:469) byte-identical to today, satisfying AC6 CLI regression

Two existing MCP soft-error return shapes (_mcp_reads.py explain_criterion, _mcp_llm.py) must gain vocabulary error codes (criterion_unknown_id/malformed_registry/missing_file, llm_unavailable) while preserving existing agent-branching fields (kind, resolution_class, retryable, diagnostic)

error_envelope.required must be relaxed from [error, input, message] to [error, message] to permit target-less failures (gate refusals not tied to a ticket) while CLI envelopes always include input and remain unchanged
